tools.name: search_trips
tools.description: Find hotels, flights and flight-and-hotel packages on Vuelo for a destination, dates and number of travellers, within a budget. The results appear in the Vuelo card, where the traveller compares and books them: do not follow up with a question asking which one they want. Hotels are live; pass origin and destinationAirport (IATA codes) to include flights and packages. Flight fares are live and ticketed at purchase. Pass cabin for premium economy, business or first. Returns prices, photos and the payment options Vuelo offers for each trip. Show payment options exactly as returned and always show the full price. Call it ONCE for what the traveller asked: every call shows another Vuelo card in the chat. Do not run extra searches for other towns, dates or budgets on your own; if the request is broad ("somewhere near London"), pick the best single destination or ask the traveller, and search again only when they ask for something different.

destination.description: Town or city, with its country when the name is shared or could be ambiguous: "Lisbon", "Zurich, Switzerland", "Cambridge, UK". A region (the Cotswolds) cannot be searched: use one town in it.

to.description: Check-out or return date, YYYY-MM-DD. For a one-way flight, give the same date as from.

origin.description: Where they fly from, to include live flights and packages: an airport code (LHR) or, when the traveller names a city, the city (London, or LON), which searches every airport there (Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted, Luton, City). Pass the city unless they named one airport. Ask where they are flying from if they want flights.

destinationAirport.description: Arrival airport for the destination, for example LIS for Lisbon; for a city with several airports (London, Paris, New York, Milan, Rome, Tokyo, Stockholm) pass the city to search them all.

only.description: What the traveller asked for. Set "flights" whenever they ask for flights and not a hotel (for example "find me flights to Nice"), "stays" for a hotel only, "packages" for flight and hotel together. Only leave it out when they want to see everything. Never add hotels to a flights request.

refundableOnly.description: Only stays with a refundable rate, when the traveller asks for refundable or free cancellation. Flights are ticketed at booking, so none are refundable.

minStars.description: Minimum hotel star rating, when the traveller asks for one (for example 5 for "5-star").

hotel.description: The hotel, when the traveller names one ("the Pulitzer", "The Savoy"): its name only, with the town in destination. Vuelo finds it by name and lists it first, with other hotels in the town after it. Never use minStars or a budget to stand in for a named hotel.

directOnly.description: Flights: only nonstop flights, when the traveller asks for direct or nonstop.

airline.description: Flights: an airline the traveller names ("Virgin", "BA"): its flights are listed first. A name or its two-letter code.

cabin.description: Which cabin to price flights in, when the traveller asks for one ("business class", "premium economy", "first"). Economy when not said. Only affects flights and packages.

passengers.description: Pass this whenever you know it: the results page and checkout then need nothing typed. Who is flying, if the traveller has already told you or you know it: full names as on the passport, and dates of birth if you have them. Vuelo fills these into the booking form so they are not asked for again. Names alone still help. This is who is flying; travellers above is how many.

mobile.description: The traveller's mobile number (any country; international format such as +1 415 555 2671 outside the UK), whenever you already know it from this conversation or about the user. Always pass it if you have it: when they tap Book in the Vuelo card, Vuelo texts the secure link straight to it, so they type nothing. Vuelo keeps it for this conversation only and never shows it in the chat. Do not ask for it just to search.

traveller.description: The person booking, whenever you know them from this conversation or about the user: full name as on their ID, email, date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD) and home postcode. Vuelo keeps them for this conversation, so when the traveller taps Book in the card they have nothing to type. Never guess any of it.

tools.name: get_hotel_availability
tools.description: Live rooms and prices at ONE hotel the traveller already has in mind, for their dates and number of guests, without searching the whole town. Pass the reference you hold: a Vuelo hotel link (https://…/h/…), an offerId from an earlier Vuelo search, a Vuelo property_id (VHP_…) or a hotel id from a Vuelo search. Use it when the traveller shares a Vuelo hotel link or asks about the same hotel on other dates. The result appears in the Vuelo card. No result means the hotel has nothing for those dates or is not one Vuelo can sell: say so, and offer to search the town. Prices hold for about an hour: book soon after, or check again.

property.description: The hotel: a Vuelo hotel link, an offerId from a Vuelo search, a Vuelo property_id (VHP_…) or a hotel id from a Vuelo search.

tools.name: get_offer
tools.description: Details, terms, photos and the payment options for one Vuelo offer, repriced live.

tools.name: get_flight_extras
tools.description: For a flight offer from search_trips, when the traveller asks about luggage or seats, or before book_trip if they want an extra bag: what the fare includes, the extra bags on sale (each with a choice_id, for which passenger by position, which way, its price and the most allowed), and for each flight how many seats can be chosen and their price range. To add bags, pass extras: [{ choice_id, quantity }] to book_trip; the traveller sees them ticked on the booking page and can change them. Seats are chosen by the traveller on the booking page, from the seat map, never here. Bags and seats cannot be added through Vuelo after booking. Prices are as listed now; the booking page shows the total.

tools.name: change_package_flight
tools.description: For a flight-and-hotel package from search_trips: every other flight for the same route and dates, each priced as a package with the same stay, with what it costs each traveller more or less than the current flight. The Vuelo card uses this for its Change flight list; call it yourself when the traveller asks for other flights for a package, then book the offerId they choose.

tools.name: book_trip
tools.description: Bookings are made under Vuelo's Booking Terms and Conditions (https://getvuelo.com/uk/legal/terms-of-booking-service/); the Vuelo card and pay page show them. Start booking a Vuelo offer, by the offerId and paymentOption that search_trips returned; call it whenever the traveller asks in the chat to book one. The Vuelo card then shows the traveller a Pay button that opens Vuelo's secure page (Apple Pay, Google Pay or a card), or, where there is no card or they ask for one, Vuelo texts them a secure link; nothing is booked until they pay. Never show a link in the chat, except a passkey approval link Vuelo returns for you to show. Pre-fill: pass everything you already know about the traveller, from this conversation or what you know about the user, so checkout is a single tap with nothing to type: leadTraveller (full name as on their ID, email, date of birth, home postcode), mobile, and for flights each passenger's name, date of birth, title and gender. Never guess or invent any of it; ask only for what Vuelo says is missing, once, in one message. Flights cannot book without each passenger's name and date of birth. To change how an open booking is paid for, use change_payment_option (calling book_trip again with another paymentOption does the same). Do not wait for the traveller to tell you they have paid: pass notify_url to hear the moment they open the link, pay or cancel, or straight after sending the link call get_booking_status with wait_seconds: 50, which answers the moment they pay. Then tell them it is booked, with the reference.

paymentOption.description: One of the options search_trips returned as eligible

title.description: As on the passport, if you know it.

gender.description: As on the passport, if you know it.

travellers.description: Each passenger, as on their passport, with their title and gender where you know them (airlines need both). If the traveller has already told you who is flying, pass them rather than making them type it again. Leave it out for a returning traveller: Vuelo fills in its own saved passengers and asks you to confirm them.

travellersConfirmed.description: Set true when the traveller has confirmed the passengers Vuelo filled in and named back to you. Vuelo asks for this once, before it starts a booking with saved passengers.

consumer_ref.description: The vc_ reference Vuelo gave you after this traveller authorised you to book for them within limits. Only if you already hold one; never ask the traveller for it, or mention it to them: they do not have one to give. With it, Vuelo books inside their limits without a payment step, or asks them to approve with their passkey. Without it, book as usual: the traveller pays with one tap on Vuelo's secure page.

mobile.description: Mobile number to text the link to (any country; international format outside the UK). Not needed for returning customers, or if you already passed it to search_trips in this conversation. If you already know it from this conversation or from what you know about the user, pass it rather than asking again: Vuelo then texts the link at once, with nothing for the traveller to type.

city.description: Town or city of their home address

leadTraveller.description: The traveller booking: name, email, date of birth and home postcode, town and county, as far as you know them. Pass whatever you already know from this conversation or about the user rather than asking: Vuelo logs them straight in, or fills in their Vuelo account so they only check it and accept Vuelo's terms. For a traveller new to Vuelo, their Vuelo account needs their name, date of birth and home postcode, town and county: pass them if you know them, or ask once before booking, so the pay page is one tap. Never invent any of it.

delivery.description: How the confirmation reaches the traveller. Leave it out: a card payment always goes by text to the traveller's mobile, and a no-card reservation by a Confirm button in the Vuelo card. qr and on_device are no longer offered and are treated as a text. Defaults to a text message, or to a Confirm button in the Vuelo card when nothing needs paying now.

from_card.description: Set only by the Vuelo card. Leave it out.

host.description: Which assistant this is, so the Vuelo page names it and matches its look. One of: chatgpt, claude, gemini, meta, instinct, openclaw, perplexity, copilot, mistral, grok, poe, duckduckgo. Optional, and an unrecognised value is simply ignored rather than refused.

payer.description: Only when the traveller says someone else is paying (a friend, a partner, a parent): their name and mobile or email, as the traveller gives them. Vuelo then sends the secure link to that person instead of the traveller; they pay in full from their own Vuelo account. Ask who is paying before booking if the traveller has mentioned it. The traveller still gets the confirmation at their own mobile, if given.

extras.description: A flight only: extra bags the traveller asked for, by choice_id from get_flight_extras. They are ticked on the booking page for the traveller to check before paying; seats are chosen there. Leave out for none.

notify_url.description: Your own https address. The moment the traveller confirms on their phone, Vuelo POSTs it a booking.confirmed event (reference, trip, dates, amount), so you can tell them without being asked. Optional.

notify_token.description: A secret of yours. Vuelo sends it back in X-Vuelo-Notify-Token and signs the event with it (X-Vuelo-Signature: sha256=HMAC). Optional.

tools.name: get_booking_progress
tools.description: Progress of the newest booking for an offer, or the newest booking of all, for the Vuelo widget.

tools.name: change_payment_option
tools.description: When the traveller wants to pay a different way (for example reserve now instead of paying in full) before they have confirmed. Switches the open booking to that paymentOption; the link already texted stays the same and opens with the new choice, so nothing new is sent. Only an option the trip lists as available.

tools.name: update_travellers
tools.description: Correct who is travelling on a booking the traveller has not paid for yet: a passenger's name or date of birth (names exactly as on the passport, dates YYYY-MM-DD). Give only what changes, by position: { passenger: 2, name: "Sophie Hougham", dateOfBirth: "1990-04-12" }. What you leave out stays as it was. The link already sent opens with the new names; nothing is resent. Refused once the traveller has paid: names on a ticket are changed with the airline through Vuelo support.

leadTraveller.description: The booking traveller's email, date of birth and home postcode, town and county, to fill in their Vuelo account on the pay page.

passenger.description: Which passenger, from 1. Left out: by order in this list.

tools.name: resend_link
tools.description: When the traveller says the secure link has not arrived, or asks for another: Vuelo texts it again, to the same number. The first time it resends the same link; after that, once it has been opened, or once it has expired, Vuelo cancels it and texts a fresh one, and only the newest works. Never pass the link on in the chat yourself. At most three links a booking.

tools.name: send_to_payer
tools.description: After a booking has started, when the traveller says someone else is paying (a friend, a partner, a parent, their company); if you know before booking, pass payer to book_trip instead. Vuelo sends that person a secure link of their own, by text, email or both. Only when the traveller asks, with the name and the mobile or email they give you: never guess or reuse a number, and confirm it with the traveller first. The payer sees the trip, the price and who asked, never the traveller's own details, and pays in full from their own Vuelo account (no payment plan). The traveller's own link stops working, so the trip cannot be paid twice; the traveller still gets the booking confirmation. The link lasts 24 hours and the price is checked when they pay. Never pass the link on in the chat yourself.

name.description: The name of the person paying, as the traveller gave it.

mobile.description: Their mobile, to text the link.

email.description: Their email, to email the link.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Cancel a Vuelo booking, before or after the traveller confirms. Pass the taskId if it was made in this conversation; from any other conversation, a made booking can be cancelled with its Vuelo reference (VU-...) and the email or mobile it was booked with. Not confirmed yet: it is called off at once, the texted link stops working and nothing was charged. Already booked: call it first with preview: true and tell the traveller what they would get back (refund.amount, summary). If they want to go ahead, call it again without preview. A reservation with nothing paid is cancelled at once. For anything paid, Vuelo texts the traveller a six-digit code and nothing is cancelled until it is given: ask them for it and call again with code (they can also enter it on their booking page). Never guess a code, and never say a paid booking is cancelled until this or get_booking_status says so.

taskId.description: The taskId book_trip returned, when the booking was made in this conversation.

email.description: With reference: the email the traveller booked with.

mobile.description: With reference, instead of email: the mobile on the booking.

preview.description: true: only say what cancelling would refund, changing nothing.

code.description: For a paid booking: the six-digit code Vuelo texted the traveller, as they gave it to you. Finishes the cancellation and the refund.

tools.name: contact_support
tools.description: Send the traveller's request to Vuelo's support team, who will be in touch with them. Use it whenever the traveller wants something done to a Vuelo booking that the other tools cannot do, or wants a person: change dates or names after paying, a refund question, a payment problem, a complaint, anything. It works in any conversation: pass the taskId if the booking was made in this chat; otherwise their Vuelo booking reference (VU-...) and the email or mobile they booked with, or just their email if they have no reference. To cancel a booking made in this chat, use cancel_booking first: it raises the request itself when Vuelo's team has to do it. Write the message in the traveller's words, with what they want and why. Tell them the ticket reference and reply time this returns.

taskId.description: The taskId book_trip returned, when the booking was made in this conversation.

reference.description: The Vuelo booking reference (VU-...), when there is no taskId.

email.description: The email the traveller booked with: needed when there is no taskId, or when this tool asks for it.

mobile.description: With reference, instead of email: the mobile on the booking.

message.description: What the traveller wants, in their words.

tools.name: find_my_booking
tools.description: For a traveller who booked with Vuelo before, in another conversation, and wants to see, change, cancel or get help with it: Vuelo texts the booking's own page to the mobile on that booking. On that page they can cancel, add it to their calendar, and contact Vuelo's team. Pass their Vuelo booking reference (VU-...) and the email or mobile they booked with. If they do not have the reference, pass the mobile they booked with alone (with country if it is not written with +): Vuelo texts that number a link to each of its latest bookings. You never see a link or whether anything matched, so tell them: if the details match, Vuelo has texted the mobile on the booking. They can also see every booking on their mobile at Vuelo's bookings page (/bookings on the site their booking links open), with a code texted to it. Never search their email or messages for a reference instead: ask for the mobile. For anything else they want a person for, use contact_support.

reference.description: The Vuelo booking reference, VU-... Leave out if the traveller does not have it, and pass the mobile alone.

email.description: The email the traveller booked with.

mobile.description: The mobile on the booking: with the reference instead of the email, or alone without the reference.

country.description: For a mobile typed the local way (06 12 34 56 78), the country it is from, as an ISO code (FR). Not needed for a number with +.

tools.name: list_my_bookings
tools.description: For a traveller who wants to manage a booking here, in the chat, and does not have its reference: every booking on the mobile they booked with. Two calls. First pass the mobile alone (with country if it is not written with +): Vuelo texts that number a 6-digit code, and the answer is the same whether or not it has bookings. Ask the traveller for the code, then call again with the same mobile and the code: you get each booking's reference, what it is, its dates, its status (booked, reserved, cancelled, awaiting_payment, payment_link_expired), and the date to pay by or to cancel free by. Show them the list and ask which one. Then use get_booking, cancel_booking or request_change with that reference and this mobile. Never names, dates of birth or booking pages. If the code is not right, ask them to check the text; after five wrong tries, call again without the code for a new one.

mobile.description: The mobile the traveller booked with.

country.description: For a mobile typed the local way (06 12 34 56 78), the country it is from, as an ISO code (FR). Not needed for a number with +.

code.description: The 6-digit code Vuelo texted, once the traveller has read it out. Leave out on the first call.

tools.name: send_receipt
tools.description: When the traveller asks for a receipt, an invoice or proof of a booking: Vuelo emails it to the email on the booking (never to an address you give), with what was booked, the dates, and the money as it stands: paid, reserved with the date it is due, on a payment plan, or cancelled with its refund. You do not see the receipt. Pass the Vuelo reference (VU-...) and the email or mobile it was booked with, or the taskId of a booking made in this conversation. If the booking has no email, it says so: then use contact_support.

email.description: The email the traveller booked with.

mobile.description: Or the mobile on the booking.

taskId.description: The booking's taskId, if it was made in this conversation.

tools.name: get_booking
tools.description: For a booking made in another conversation, or through another assistant: where it stands, by its Vuelo reference (VU-...) and the email or mobile it was booked with. Says booked, reserved, cancelled, cancellation_in_progress or not_booked, with the item, dates, number of travellers, amount, free cancellation date, the stay (hotel, area, stars, room, nights, what is included, any tax paid at the hotel, and a public page about the hotel), the date a reservation must be paid by, any requests with Vuelo's team, and its history oldest first (booked or reserved, cancellation_requested, cancelled, refund_sent, request_raised, team_replied, changed with what changed, request_resolved). It never gives names, dates of birth or the booking page: to give the traveller their page, use find_my_booking. If nothing matches, say the details did not match a booking and ask them to check the reference and the email or mobile; never say which was wrong. For a booking made in this conversation, use get_booking_status.

email.description: The email the traveller booked with.

mobile.description: Or the mobile on the booking, instead of the email.

tools.name: request_change
tools.description: A change to a paid booking, which no tool can make directly: a name on a ticket goes through the airline, and new dates or flights are re-booked by Vuelo's team. Sends the change typed, so the team acts on exactly what the traveller wants, and returns a ticket reference and reply time to tell them. Nothing changes until the team does it, so never say it has. kind passenger_details: passenger (position, from 1), field (name, date_of_birth, title or gender) and new_value (a name exactly as on the passport, or YYYY-MM-DD). kind dates: new_from and new_to. kind flight: which (outbound or return) and new_value. kind special_request (a request to the hotel): request (late_check_in, early_check_in, accessibility, cot, connecting_rooms, bed_type, dietary or other), new_value for a time or bed (e.g. 'arriving 23:30', 'twin beds') and notes; the hotel decides, so say it has been asked for, never that it is confirmed. kind room or other: notes. Before paying, use update_travellers or book again instead. By the Vuelo reference (VU-...) and the email or mobile it was booked with.

email.description: The email the traveller booked with.

mobile.description: Or the mobile on the booking, instead of the email.

request.description: For kind special_request: what to ask the hotel for.

tools.name: follow_up_ticket
tools.description: When the traveller asks you to check a support request later ("check it later today", "let me know tomorrow"): you cannot come back by yourself, so Vuelo does. Pass the ticket reference (SUP-...), how many hours from now to check (in_hours, 1 to 72; 4 if they just say later today), and the taskId of the booking in this conversation or the email or mobile the request was raised with. At that time Vuelo checks the request and texts the traveller where it stands, with any refund or cancellation; if the team replies sooner, Vuelo texts them then. Tell the traveller when Vuelo will text. Up to three checks a day per request.

in_hours.description: Hours from now to check. 4 for "later today", 24 for "tomorrow".

taskId.description: The booking's taskId, if it was made in this conversation.

email.description: The email the request was raised with.

mobile.description: Or the mobile on the request.

tools.name: get_support_ticket
tools.description: Where a request to Vuelo's support team stands: with the team, replied (the reply is in the traveller's email), or resolved. Pass the ticket reference (SUP-...) and either the taskId of the booking in this conversation or the email the traveller gave. Use it when the traveller asks for an update. To add to a request, call contact_support again with the same booking and reason: it joins the same conversation.

taskId.description: The booking's taskId, if it was made in this conversation.

email.description: The email the traveller gave for the reply.

mobile.description: Or the mobile on the request.

tools.name: get_booking_status
tools.description: The current state of a Vuelo booking started with book_trip. Pass wait_seconds (up to 50) straight after the traveller has the link: it answers the moment they open it, pay or cancel, so you can tell them it is booked without being told.

wait_seconds.description: Hold the answer until the booking changes, up to this many seconds.
